p.src: Now Shi Xiangyun ran outside, afraid that Lin Daiyu would catch her, while Baoyu hurriedly called from behind, “Take care you don't trip! How could she possibly catch you?” When Lin Daiyu reached the doorway, Baoyu barred her way with his arms braced against the doorframe and smilingly urged, “Let her off this once.” Trying to pull his hands away, Lin Daiyu said, “If I let Yun'er off, may I drop dead!” Seeing Baoyu blocking the doorway and realizing that Daiyu could not get out, Xiangyun stopped and laughed, “Dear sister, please let me off this once.” Just then Baochai came up behind Xiangyun and said with a smile, “For Brother Bao's sake, I advise you both to let the matter drop.” “I won't,” said Daiyu. “You are all in league together, making sport of me!” Baoyu protested, “Who would dare make sport of you? If you had not teased her, how would she have dared say anything about you?” While the four were still hopelessly entangled in their dispute, someone came to summon them to the meal, and only then did they go to the front rooms. That evening, when the lamps were lit, Lady Wang, Li Wan, Xifeng, Yingchun, Tanchun, Xichun, and the others all gathered in Grandmother Jia's apartments. After chatting for a while, each retired for the night. Xiangyun again went to sleep in Daiyu's room.

p.src: Baoyu escorted the two girls to their room. It was already past the second watch, and only after Xiren had come several times to hurry him did he return to his own room to sleep. At daybreak the next morning, he threw on his clothes, slipped his feet into his shoes, and went to Daiyu's room. Zijuan and Cuilü were nowhere to be seen; only the two girls still lay beneath the covers. Lin Daiyu was wrapped snugly in an apricot-red satin quilt, sleeping peacefully with her eyes closed. Shi Xiangyun, by contrast, had a mass of black hair trailing beside her pillow, her quilt drawn only to her breast, and one snow-white arm, adorned with two gold bracelets, flung outside it. At the sight, Baoyu sighed, “Even in your sleep you can't behave yourself! Later, when the wind chills you, you'll complain that your shoulder aches again.” As he spoke, he gently covered her arm. Lin Daiyu was already awake. Sensing someone there, she guessed it must be Baoyu; when she rolled over to look, she found that she was right. She asked, “What have you come running over here so early for?” Baoyu laughed. “It isn't early at all! Get up and see for yourself.” Daiyu said, “Go outside first and let us get dressed.” Hearing this, Baoyu turned and went outside.

p.src: Daiyu rose and woke Xiangyun, and they both dressed. Baoyu then came back in and sat beside the dressing table, while Zijuan and Xueyan entered to attend the girls as they washed and dressed. When Xiangyun had washed her face, Cuilü picked up the basin to throw out the remaining water. Baoyu said, “Wait. I'll wash in it while it's here and save myself the trouble of going back.” So saying, he came over, bent down, and splashed his face a couple of times. Zijuan handed him the scented soap, but Baoyu said, “There is plenty of it already in the water. I needn't rub on any more.” After splashing his face twice more, he asked for a towel. Cuilü said, “Still that same old habit! When will you ever change?” Baoyu ignored her. He hurriedly asked for some green salt, cleaned his teeth, and rinsed his mouth. When he had finished and saw that Xiangyun's hair was already done, he went over and said with a smile, “Dear sister, please do my hair for me.” “I can't do that now,” replied Xiangyun. Baoyu laughed. “Dear sister, how is it that you used to do it for me?” Xiangyun said, “I've forgotten how now, so how am I to do it?” Baoyu said, “I'm not going out anyway, and I shan't wear a cap or headband. Just make a few loose braids, and that will do.” Then he pleaded with her over and over, calling her his dear sister. Xiangyun had no choice but to draw his head toward her and comb it carefully through. At home Baoyu wore no cap, nor did he bind his hair into the twin tufts of boyhood. Instead, the short hair around his head was made into little braids, gathered together with the hair at the crown into one large braid, and tied with a red cord. Four pearls were set at intervals from the crown to the tip of the braid, with a gold pendant hanging below. As she braided his hair, Xiangyun said, “There are only three of the proper pearls here; this one doesn't match. I remember all four being alike. How did one go missing?” “I lost one,” said Baoyu. Xiangyun said, “It must have fallen off while you were out. Someone probably picked it up and got a fine windfall.” Washing her hands nearby, Daiyu sneered, “Who knows whether it was truly lost, or whether it was given to someone to have set in some ornament to wear!” Baoyu made no reply. The dressing table was flanked by cosmetic cases and other such things, and he casually picked them up to admire them. Before he knew it, his hand had taken up some rouge, which he was about to put to his lips, though he hesitated for fear that Shi Xiangyun would scold him. While he was still wavering, Xiangyun indeed spotted him from behind. Holding his braid aside with one hand, she reached out with the other and smacked the rouge from his fingers. “When will you ever cure yourself of this incorrigible habit?” she demanded.

p.src: Before she had finished speaking, Xiren came in. Seeing the scene before her, she understood that Baoyu had already washed and dressed, and could only go back to attend to her own toilet. Presently Baochai came in and asked, “Where has Brother Bao gone?” Xiren replied with a smile, “When does Brother Bao ever have time to stay in his own room?” Baochai understood her meaning at once. Then she heard Xiren sigh, “It is well for brothers and sisters to be affectionate, but there should still be some sense of propriety and decorum. No one ought to carry on like this day and night! No matter how anyone advises him, it all goes in one ear and out the other.” Hearing this, Baochai thought to herself, “I must not underestimate this maid. Judging by the way she speaks, she has considerable good sense.” Baochai sat down on the kang and, in the course of leisurely conversation, gradually drew her out about her age, native place, and other matters. Observing her closely, Baochai found her speech and aspirations deeply worthy of respect and affection.

p.src: Before long Baoyu returned, just as Baochai was leaving. Baoyu asked Xiren, “What were you and Cousin Bao talking about so merrily? Why did she run off the moment I came in?” She did not answer the first time he asked. When he asked again, Xiren finally said, “Are you asking me? How should I know what is going on between you?” Hearing this and seeing that her expression was quite unlike its usual self, Baoyu smiled and said, “Why are you truly angry?” Xiren gave a cold laugh. “How would I dare be angry! Only, from now on, you had better not come into this room again. You have others to wait on you in any case, so do not order me about anymore. I shall go back to serving the Old Lady as before.” As she spoke, she lay down on the kang and closed her eyes. Baoyu was deeply astonished by this behavior and could not help hurrying over to soothe her. But Xiren merely kept her eyes shut and ignored him. At a loss, Baoyu saw Sheyue come in and asked, “What is the matter with your elder sister?” Sheyue replied, “How should I know? Ask yourself and you will understand.” Baoyu stared blankly for a while. Feeling rebuffed, he rose with a sigh and said, “Ignore me, then. I shall go to sleep too.” With that, he got down from the kang and flung himself upon his own bed. After hearing no movement from him for some time, only a faint snore, Xiren supposed he had fallen asleep. She rose, fetched a cloak, and had just laid it over him when, with a sudden swish, Baoyu flung it aside, then kept his eyes closed and pretended to sleep. Knowing perfectly well what he meant, Xiren nodded and said with a cold smile, “You need not be angry either. From now on I shall pretend to be mute and never say another word to you. Will that suit you?” Unable to contain himself, Baoyu sat up and asked, “What have I done now? You say you have admonished me again. It would be one thing if you had, but just now I never saw you admonish me at all. The moment I came in, you ignored me and lay down in a huff. I still cannot fathom why, and now you say that I am angry. When did I ever hear you offer me any advice?” Xiren said, “If you still do not understand in your own heart, must you wait for me to spell it out?” While they were still quarreling, the Lady Dowager sent someone to call him to dinner. He went to the front apartments, hastily ate half a bowlful, and returned to his room. There he found Xiren lying on the kang in the outer room while Sheyue polished dominoes beside her. Baoyu knew that Sheyue and Xiren were very close, so he ignored Sheyue as well, lifted the soft curtain, and went into the inner room by himself. Sheyue had no choice but to follow him inside. Baoyu pushed her out, saying, “I would not dare trouble any of you.” Sheyue could only come out smiling and send two young maids inside. Baoyu took up a book and read reclining for quite some time. When he wanted tea, he looked up and saw only the two young maids standing on the floor.

p.src: The elder of the two was exceptionally fresh and pretty, so Baoyu asked, “What is your name?” The maid replied, “Huixiang.” Baoyu asked, “Who gave you that name?” Huixiang said, “I was originally called Yunxiang. Elder Sister Hua changed it to Huixiang.” Baoyu said, “You ought properly to be called ‘Huìqì—Ill Luck’! What sort of name is Huixiang?” Then he asked, “How many sisters are there in your family?” “Four,” replied Huixiang. “Which one are you?” asked Baoyu. “The fourth,” said Huixiang. Baoyu said, “From tomorrow onward you shall be called Si'er, ‘Number Four.’ There is no need for names like ‘Fragrant Orchid’ or ‘Orchid Breath.’ Which one of them is worthy of comparison with such flowers? Fine names are only sullied for nothing.” As he spoke, he ordered her to pour him some tea. Hearing this from the outer room, Xiren and Sheyue pursed their lips to hide their smiles.

p.src: That day Baoyu scarcely left his room or romped with the young ladies and maids. He remained in low spirits, merely reading to dispel his gloom or amusing himself with brush and ink. He called on none of the others, asking only Si'er to attend him.

p.src: As it happened, Si'er was an exceptionally clever and engaging maid. Seeing that Baoyu had chosen to employ her, she devised every possible means of winning his favor. After the evening meal, Baoyu drank two cups of wine. As his eyes grew drowsy and his ears warm, he remembered how in former days Xiren and the others would all have been there, laughing and making merry. Tonight, however, he sat alone before the lamp in desolate silence and found it utterly cheerless. He thought of driving them away, yet feared that this would please them and make them admonish him all the more in future. But to invoke his authority as master and intimidate them with rules would seem far too heartless. There was nothing for it but to harden his heart and regard them as dead; life would have to go on regardless. If he simply treated them as dead, he would have no ties or cares and could instead take serene pleasure in himself. He therefore ordered Si'er to trim the lamp and brew tea while he read the Nanhua Classic for a while. He had just reached the passage entitled “Rifling Trunks” in the Outer Chapters, which read:

p.src: Therefore, abolish sagehood and discard wisdom, and the great thieves will cease; cast away jade and destroy pearls, and petty thieves will not arise; burn tallies and break seals, and the people will become simple and unassuming; smash measures and break scales, and the people will cease contending; utterly destroy the sagely laws of the world, and only then may the people be reasoned with. Confound the six pitch-pipes, melt down and destroy the mouth organs and zithers, stop the ears of the blind musician Kuang, and only then will all beneath heaven retain their own keenness of hearing; Obliterate patterns and designs, scatter the five colors, seal the eyes of Li Zhu, and only then will all beneath heaven retain their own clarity of sight; destroy measuring cords, cast away compass and square, and crush the fingers of the craftsman Chui, and only then will all beneath heaven possess their own skill.

p.src: Burn Hua and scatter She, and only then will those in the women's chambers retain their admonitions; maim Baochai's immortal beauty and reduce Daiyu's inspired intelligence to ashes; extinguish and diminish affection, and only then will beauty and ugliness in the women's chambers resemble each other. If they retain their admonitions, there will be no fear of estrangement; if her immortal beauty is maimed, there will be no heart inclined to love; if her inspired intelligence is reduced to ashes, there will be no feeling born of literary talent. Those Chai, Yu, Hua, and She all spread their nets and burrow their tunnels; by these means they bewilder, entangle, and ensnare all the world.

p.src: When he had finished, he tossed aside his brush and went to bed. No sooner had his head touched the pillow than he fell fast asleep, knowing nothing throughout the night, and did not wake until dawn. Turning over, he saw Xiren lying asleep atop the quilt, still fully dressed. Baoyu had already put the events of the previous day out of his mind. He nudged her and said, “Get up and sleep properly, or you will catch cold.” Xiren had seen that he fooled about with the girls at all hours of the day and night. Knowing that direct remonstrance would never reform him, she had used tender affection to warn him, expecting that within half a day, or even a few moments, he would return to his usual self. Unexpectedly, Baoyu remained unmoved for a whole day and night, leaving her at a loss, so that she herself had scarcely slept all night. Now, seeing Baoyu behave this way, she guessed that his heart had softened and deliberately ignored him all the more. When she did not answer, Baoyu reached out to undress her. He had just undone one button when Xiren pushed his hand away and fastened it again herself. At his wits’ end, Baoyu took her hand and asked with a smile, “What on earth is wrong with you?” After he had asked several times, Xiren opened her eyes and said, “Nothing is wrong with me. Now that you are awake, go to the other room and wash and dress yourself. If you delay any longer, you will miss it.” “Where am I supposed to go?” asked Baoyu. Xiren gave a cold laugh. “Why ask me? How should I know? Go wherever you please. From now on, let us have nothing more to do with each other, and spare ourselves these ceaseless squabbles that make others laugh. Whenever you tire of the people over there and come back here, there will always be some ‘Si’er’ or ‘Wu’er’ to wait on you. As for creatures like us, we have merely ‘brought disgrace upon our fine names and worthy surnames.’” Baoyu laughed. “Are you still remembering that today?” “I shall remember it for a hundred years!” said Xiren. I am not like you, who let my words go in one ear and out the other—told something at night, you have forgotten it by morning.” Seeing her face full of pretty indignation, Baoyu could no longer contain his feelings. He picked up a jade hairpin from beside the pillow and snapped it in two, saying, “If ever I fail to heed you again, may I end up just like this.” Xiren hurriedly picked up the broken hairpin. “Why do such a thing first thing in the morning? Whether you listen or not is hardly so important that you should behave like this.” “You have no idea how anxious I feel!” said Baoyu. Xiren smiled. “So you do know what it is to be anxious! Then can you imagine how I have felt? Hurry up, get out of bed, and wash your face.” With that, the two of them finally rose and washed and dressed.

From now on, let us have nothing more to do with each other, and spare ourselves these ceaseless squabbles that make others laugh.
Whenever you tire of the people over there and come back here, there will always be some ‘Si’er’ or ‘Wu’er’ to wait on you.
As for creatures like us, we have merely ‘brought disgrace upon our fine names and worthy surnames.’”
Baoyu laughed. “Are you still remembering that today?”
“I shall remember it for a hundred years!” said Xiren.
I am not like you, who let my words go in one ear and out the other—told something at night, you have forgotten it by morning.”

Seeing her face full of pretty indignation, Baoyu could no longer contain his feelings. He picked up a jade hairpin from beside the pillow and snapped it in two, saying, “If ever I fail to heed you again, may I end up just like this.”
Xiren hurriedly picked up the broken hairpin. “Why do such a thing first thing in the morning?
Whether you listen or not is hardly so important that you should behave like this.”
“You have no idea how anxious I feel!” said Baoyu.
Xiren smiled. “So you do know what it is to be anxious!
Then can you imagine how I have felt?
Hurry up, get out of bed, and wash your face.”
With that, the two of them finally rose and washed and dressed.

p.src: As it happened, Fengjie’s daughter, Dajie, had fallen ill, and everyone was in a turmoil summoning a physician to feel her pulse. The physician said, “Please offer my congratulations to the ladies. The young miss’s fever means the happy visitation of smallpox; it is no other illness.” On hearing this, Lady Wang and Fengjie hurriedly sent someone to ask, “Will she recover safely?” The physician replied, “Though the illness is dangerous, it is progressing normally, so there should be no great harm. The important thing is to prepare mulberry worms and pigs’ tails.” At once Fengjie busied herself: she had the rooms swept and an altar prepared for the Smallpox Goddess; ordered the household to abstain from fried and sautéed foods; instructed Ping’er to pack bedding and clothes so that Jia Lian could sleep elsewhere; and brought out lengths of bright-red cloth to make garments for the wet nurses, maids, and other close attendants. Outside, a clean room was also prepared to lodge two physicians, who were to take turns deliberating, feeling the patient’s pulse, and prescribing medicines; for twelve days they were not permitted to return home. Jia Lian had no choice but to move into the outer study and observe abstinence, while Fengjie and Ping’er accompanied Lady Wang in making daily offerings to the goddess.

p.src: Now Jia Lian could never be apart from Fengjie without getting into mischief. After sleeping alone for two nights, he found the strain intolerable and temporarily selected the more handsome among the young male servants to relieve his desires. There was in the Rong mansion an utterly worthless, drunken wreck of a cook named Duoguan. Because people found him weak and incompetent, they all called him “Duohunchong,” or Duoguan the Dolt. When he was young, his parents had arranged for him to marry a woman from outside the household. She was now about twenty and possessed considerable beauty, so that no one who saw her failed to admire and desire her. By nature she was frivolous and delighted above all in flirting and making conquests. Duohunchong never objected: so long as he had wine, meat, and money, he cared about nothing else. Thus men in both the Rong and Ning mansions had succeeded in having their way with her. Because this wife was exceptionally beautiful and incomparably wanton, everyone called her “Miss Duo.” Now Jia Lian was suffering in his lonely quarters. He had seen this woman before and been utterly bewitched by her, but fear of his formidable wife at home and of her favored lovers outside had prevented him from making his move. Miss Duo had also cast her eye on Jia Lian, but had regretted never finding an opportunity. When she heard that Jia Lian had moved into the outer study, she began going by once or twice even when she had no business there, merely to entice him. She tantalized Jia Lian until he was like a starving rat. Inevitably he conferred with his trusted young servants, enlisting them to conceal the affair and help arrange it, with liberal promises of money and silk. Naturally the servants had no reason to refuse; besides, they were all on intimate terms with the woman, so the affair was arranged as soon as it was proposed. That night, at the second watch, when everyone had settled down, Duohunchong lay dead drunk on the kang, and Jia Lian slipped in for their tryst. The moment he entered and beheld her charms, his soul seemed to fly from his body. Without wasting time on endearments or tender conversation, they undressed and set to work. This woman, however, possessed a strange inborn allure: as soon as a man pressed against her, every sinew and bone in her body seemed to melt, making him feel as though he lay upon soft cotton. Her wanton gestures and lewd talk surpassed even those of a prostitute; what man reaching such a point would still care for his life? Jia Lian wished that his whole body might melt into hers. The woman deliberately spoke wantonly from beneath him: “Your daughter has broken out in smallpox, and the goddess is being worshiped at your home. You ought to observe abstinence for a couple of days, yet here you are defiling yourself because of me. Hurry and leave this place of mine.” Still thrusting vigorously, Jia Lian replied between gasps, “You are the goddess! Why should I care about any other goddess?” The more wanton the woman became, the more completely Jia Lian exposed his disgraceful behavior. When at last they had finished, the two swore eternal devotion to each other and could scarcely bear to part; from then on, they became constant lovers.

p.src: One day, after the young lady's fever had wholly subsided and her rash had faded, and twelve more days had passed, the Goddess of Smallpox was ceremonially sent away. The entire household offered sacrifices to Heaven and the ancestors, burned incense in fulfillment of their vows, held celebrations, and distributed rewards; when all this was done, Jia Lian moved back into the bedchamber. When he saw Xifeng again, it was just as the proverb says: “A reunion after long separation is sweeter than a new marriage.” Their renewed tenderness was boundless and need not be described at length.

p.src: Early the next morning, after Xifeng had gone to the main apartments, Ping'er was putting away the clothes and bedding Jia Lian had used outside when, to her surprise, she shook a lock of black hair from a pillowcase. Understanding at once, Ping'er hurriedly slipped it into her sleeve, went into the room where Jia Lian was, took out the hair, and asked him with a smile, “What is this?” The sight of it threw Jia Lian into a panic, and he lunged forward to snatch it. Ping'er ran, but Jia Lian caught her, pinned her on the kang, and tried to pry open her hand, laughing as he said, “You little hussy! If you don't hand it over this instant, I'll wrench your arm till it breaks.” Ping'er laughed. “You truly are heartless. I was kind enough to hide it from her and come ask you about it, yet you threaten me! Go on threatening me, then. When she comes back, I'll tell her and see what you do!” At this Jia Lian hastily put on a coaxing smile and pleaded, “Be a dear and give it to me. I promise I won't threaten you again.”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Xifeng's voice was heard approaching. Hearing her, Jia Lian released his grip. Ping'er had only just risen when Xifeng entered and ordered her to open the chest quickly and find a pattern for Lady Wang. Ping'er promptly assented and began searching. On seeing Jia Lian, Xifeng suddenly remembered something and asked Ping'er, “Have all the things that were taken outside been brought back in?” “Yes, they've all been brought in,” said Ping'er. “Nothing missing?” asked Xifeng. “I was afraid one or two things might have been left behind, so I checked everything carefully. Nothing is missing.” “Good, so long as nothing is missing,” said Xifeng. “But nothing extra has turned up, I hope?” Ping'er laughed. “We're lucky nothing was lost. Who would have added anything?” Xifeng gave a cold laugh. “After this past fortnight, there's no telling whether everything remained aboveboard. Some intimate friend might have left something behind—a ring, a handkerchief, a scented sachet, or even hair or fingernails. Those are things too.” At these words Jia Lian's face turned ashen. Standing behind Xifeng, Jia Lian stared at Ping'er, frantically drawing a finger across his throat and making desperate signals with his eyes. Ping'er merely pretended not to see and said with a smile, “How is it that my thoughts are exactly the same as yours, madam? I was afraid there might be something of that sort, so I searched with particular care, but I found not the slightest suspicious trace. If you don't believe me, madam, I haven't put those things away yet. You may go through them yourself.” Xifeng laughed. “Silly girl! Even if he had such things, do you imagine he would let us find them?” With that, she found the pattern and went back to the main apartments.

p.src: Ping'er pointed at her own nose, shook her head, and asked with a smile, “How are you going to repay me for this?” Jia Lian was so delighted he could hardly contain himself. He rushed forward and embraced her, calling her his “heart and soul” and thanking her over and over. Still holding the hair, Ping'er laughed. “This will give me leverage over you for the rest of my life. Treat me well and all will be well; treat me badly and I'll expose the whole affair.” Jia Lian laughed. “Then keep it safely, but whatever you do, don't let her know.” Even as he spoke, he caught her off guard and snatched it away. “It's bound to cause trouble while you have it,” he said with a laugh. “I had better burn it and be done with it.” As he spoke, he tucked it into the side of his boot. Ping'er clenched her teeth. “You heartless wretch! No sooner are you across the river than you tear down the bridge—and tomorrow you'll expect me to lie for you again!” Her pretty, provocative anger inflamed Jia Lian, and he caught her in his arms and sought to make love to her. Ping'er wrenched herself free and ran off, leaving him bent double with frustration as he cursed, “You wicked, teasing little slut! You deliberately kindle a man's fire and then run away.” From outside the window Ping'er laughed. “I may flirt as I please; who told you to get inflamed? Why should I let you enjoy yourself once, only to have her find out and take a dislike to me?” “You needn't be afraid of her,” said Jia Lian. “One day, when my temper rises, I'll smash that jar of vinegar to pieces; then she'll learn who I am! She guards against me as if I were a thief. She may talk to men, but I may not speak to women. If I so much as go near a woman, she grows suspicious; yet she jokes and laughs with brothers-in-law and nephews, old and young alike, without fearing that I might be jealous. From now on, I won't allow her to see anyone either!” Ping'er said, “She has reason to be jealous of you, but you have none to be jealous of her. She has always behaved properly and honorably, whereas whenever you do anything, you harbor some wicked intention. Even I don't trust you, let alone her.” Jia Lian said, “You two thieves sing exactly the same tune. Everything you two do is right, while every move I make is prompted by wickedness. One of these days you'll both die by my hand!”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, Xifeng entered the courtyard. Seeing Ping'er outside the window, she asked, “If you two want to talk, why don't you talk together inside? What is the meaning of one of you running outside and speaking through the window?” From inside the window Jia Lian answered, “Ask her. You would think there was a tiger in here waiting to eat her.” Ping'er said, “There was no one else in the room. What business had I staying alone with him?” Xifeng laughed. “That's precisely what makes it ideal.” At this Ping'er said, “Was that meant for me?” “Who else would I mean?” Xifeng replied with a laugh. Ping'er said, “Don't provoke me into saying something you won't like.” With that, instead of holding up the curtain for Xifeng, she flung it aside, went in first, and disappeared into the other part of the rooms. Xifeng lifted the curtain herself and entered, saying, “Ping'er has gone mad. That hussy truly means to subdue me. She had better watch her hide!” Hearing this, Jia Lian collapsed on the kang, clapping his hands and laughing. “I never knew Ping'er could be so formidable. From now on, I shall submit to her.” “It is you who have spoiled her,” said Xifeng. “I'll settle this with you!” Jia Lian hastily replied, “Whenever you two fall out, you make me the scapegoat.
